page: Google Cloud Platform g4-standard-96 is a graphics and compute-focused virtual machine belonging to the GPU Machines family. The server provides 96 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs alongside 360.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 3.75 GB of RAM per virtual core. Hardware acceleration is delivered by two NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPUs from the Blackwell family, offering a combined 192 GB of total GPU video memory. The instance does not include bundled local storage disks, requiring external network block storage for operating system images and persistent operational data. Public IPv4 networking addresses are not bundled complimentary with the provisioned host.

The primary resource focus centers on pairing high host compute capacity with substantial graphics memory. Having two high-tier workstation GPUs equipped with 192 GB aggregate VRAM allows the system to hold very large visual datasets, neural network weights, or 3D scene graphs in fast accelerator memory simultaneously. Dedicated host CPU allocations prevent resource contention across virtual cores, stabilizing multi-threaded preprocess pipelines and simulation runtimes. The lack of integrated local NVMe disks creates an architectural dependency on external volume throughput and IOPS limits for data staging.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the g4-standard-96 aggregates dual Blackwell-generation professional GPUs with an expansive host configuration, preventing the need to provision distributed multi-instance clusters for workloads demanding up to 192 GB of graphical memory. Because memory and compute are scaled broadly, the instance is targeted specifically at high-intensity tasks where single-machine GPU coordination is required. Key workloads include large-scale graphics rendering, virtual workstation virtualization, computer-aided engineering, 3D modeling pipelines, and multi-GPU deep learning inference.
description: Google Cloud Platform g4-standard-96 is an accelerator-oriented virtual machine within the GPU Machines family, engineered for intensive graphical computing and workstation workloads. It features 96 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs and 360.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 3.75 GB per core ratio. Acceleration is powered by two NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPUs based on the Blackwell architecture, providing an aggregate 192 GB of GPU VRAM. The instance includes no integrated local storage disks, necessitating external network-attached volumes for data retention and system bootstrapping, and does not provide complimentary public IPv4 addresses. By consolidating dense CPU parallelism with dual professional GPUs, g4-standard-96 suits high-fidelity graphics rendering, virtual design workstations, complex 3D simulation, and machine learning inference deployments.
